security_audit.summary: Review found no prompt-injection text or hidden malicious instructions in SKILL.md. Many static backtick and URL hits are Markdown formatting, model identifiers, placeholders, or documentation links. The remaining concerns are intentional use of the belt CLI for remote media processing and optional installation of additional third-party skills.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before examples that portrait, voice, script, audio, and video inputs may be sent to external inference providers.
Require explicit user confirmation before npx skills add commands and document trusted sources or pinned refs for related skills.
State that belt login, belt app run, and belt app store commands should run only after reviewing inputs and expected costs.
Use neutral placeholders such as your-image-url and remind users not to use media without rights or consent.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast avatar videos without building a custom media pipeline. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through belt CLI workflows for talking-head, lip sync, and dubbing videos.
actual_capabilities: Runs belt CLI workflows for P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, LatentSync, Whisper, and TTS models.
Shows text-to-avatar examples using portrait images, scripts, voices, language, prompts, and resolution settings.
Describes audio-driven avatar creation with external audio URLs.
Combines image generation, speech generation, and avatar generation into multi-step workflows.
Covers UGC-style presenter batches and localized dubbing workflows.
limitations: Requires inference.sh belt CLI access and login before commands can run.
Sends media and script inputs to external model providers.
Does not verify model pricing, availability, output rights, or moderation rules.
Example URLs are placeholders and must be replaced with user-owned assets.

use_cases.title: Create Product Presenter Videos
use_cases.description: Turn a product script and approved portrait into short talking-head videos for demos, launches, or paid social tests.

use_cases.title: Produce Course Explainers
use_cases.description: Generate consistent presenter clips for lessons, onboarding, and internal training without recording new camera footage.

use_cases.title: Localize Existing Videos
use_cases.description: Plan transcription, translation, speech generation, and lip sync steps for dubbing videos into another language.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Avatar Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-second talking-head video from my portrait URL and script. Use P-Video-Avatar, English, 720p, and a calm voice.

prompt_templates.title: UGC Product Ad
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a UGC-style avatar ad for this product. Suggest portrait style, voice, voice prompt, video prompt, and final belt workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Localized Lip Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this source video into a dubbed lip sync workflow for Spanish. Include transcription, translation, TTS, and syncing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Presenter Batch Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch process for five presenter variants. Use different voices and prompts, explain consent checks, and minimize repeated configuration.

output_examples.input: I have a portrait image and a product walkthrough script.
output: Recommended model: P-Video-Avatar for built-in speech and fast preview generation.
Input checklist: approved portrait, final script, target language, desired voice, and output resolution.
Next step: run a short test clip before producing the full video.

output_examples.input: I need to dub an existing training video into another language.
output: Workflow: transcribe the source, translate the text, generate new speech, then sync the video to the new audio.
Privacy note: confirm the video and voice data may be processed by external services.

output_examples.input: I want several UGC-style avatar variants for an ad test.
output: Plan: create one approved base script, choose several presenter voices, and vary tone and setting prompts.
Quality gate: review one sample before batching more presenters.

best_practices: Use user-owned portraits, audio, and scripts, and get written consent for likeness and voice use.
Review every belt command, estimated cost, and output destination before running it.
Start with short 720p tests before creating long or high-resolution videos.
anti_patterns: Do not create synthetic endorsements, impersonations, or influencer content without permission and disclosure.
Do not upload confidential videos, employee voices, or customer images without approval.
Do not batch-generate paid media before testing one clip for quality and policy fit.

faq.question: Does this skill require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows use the inference.sh belt CLI and require access to that service.

faq.question: Can it create speech from text?
faq.answer: Yes. P-Video-Avatar includes built-in TTS, and the guide also shows separate TTS workflows.

faq.question: Which model should I start with?
faq.answer: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar for speed, cost, built-in speech, and simple setup.

faq.question: Can it dub existing videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines transcription, translation, speech generation, and lip sync steps for dubbing workflows.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI workflows. Users should review and confirm commands before execution.

faq.question: Can I use real people in avatar videos?
faq.answer: Use real people only with permission, proper rights, and clear disclosure when synthetic media is published.
